newsitem.title: USA: Kato Kaelin takes stand in Simpson civil trial.
newsitem.headline: Kato Kaelin takes stand in Simpson civil trial.

text.p: Brian "Kato" Kaelin, O.J. Simpson's one-time house guest who became a minor celebrity during the ex-football star's criminal trial, took centre stage on Tuesday as he testified in Simpson's civil trial.

The jury in the wrongful death civil case also heard a secretly taped conversation in which Nicole Brown Simpson told police she feared Simpson might kill her when he burst into her home on Oct. 25, 1993.
"I always felt if it happened one more time it would be the last time," she told officers, explaining why she had called the police emergency number.
Kaelin appeared nervous on the witness stand as he was questioned by Daniel Petrocelli, the lead attorney for the plaintiffs.

Adding to his criminal trial testimony, he described thumps he heard on the wall of his room on the night of June 12, 1994, when Simpson's ex-wife and her friend, Ronald Goldman, were murdered, as "like someone falling back behind my bedroom wall."
A bloody glove matching one found at the murder scene was discovered in an alley behind Simpson's mansion where Kaelin said he had heard three loud thumps.

Police claimed the thumps were made by Simpson as he jumped over a fence onto his property after committing the murders. But his criminal defence team contended the glove was planted by Detective Mark Fuhrman, who they painted as a racist, rogue cop out to frame Simpson.
Simpson was found not guilty of the murders in October, 1995 and is now fighting the wrongful death lawsuit brought by the victims' families, who are seeking financial damages.

Kaelin also testified that he and Simpson watched a video on Oct. 25, 1993 which contained a scene involving oral sex and which Simpson compared to an act he had witnessed his wife performing on another man. According to previous testimony, what Simpson saw sparked the fight later that day.

On an audiotape made while Simpson was still in Nicole Brown Simpson's home that night, with a tape recorder hidden in the pocket of Sgt. Craig Lally, Nicole Brown Simpson said Simpson "gets this animalistic look to him and I get scared when he looks like that."
The tape was not played to the jury in his criminal trial.
Simpson is heard on the tape expressing surprise that his then-estranged wife had called the police. "We were yelling at each other but I'm surprised she called the cops."
Asked what started the fight, he said "An ex-boyfriend." Later Simpson said, "I didn't want this guy in her life."

Nicole Brown Simpson said Simpson had called her several times on the evening of Oct. 25 and she finally hung up on him and took the phone off the hook. "That's when he came over and kicked the door down," she said.
